claims.claim: The listed defenses are common in consumer debt lawsuits.
The debt being too old is a defense.
claims.quote: When the period in which an action must be commenced under this section has run, a person shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect the debt. The period in which an action may be commenced under this section shall only be extended pursuant to Section 360.
claims.note: The test is whether the applicable period has expired for an action covered by this section, not simply the age of the debt.

claims.claim: The plaintiff's inability to show it owns the debt is a defense.
claims.note: Section 431.30 addresses denials, not what a plaintiff must prove about ownership.

claims.claim: The plaintiff's inability to show the amount of the debt is a defense.
claims.note: No source specifies what the plaintiff must prove about the amount.

claims.claim: The debt not being yours is a defense.
claims.quote: (1) The general or specific denial of the material allegations of the complaint controverted by the defendant.
claims.note: This supports denying an allegation that the defendant owes the debt. It does not identify mistaken identity as a separate defense.
Neither source addresses service or how to challenge it.

claims.claim: A defense that is not raised can be lost.
claims.quote: (2) A statement of any new matter constituting a defense.
claims.note: The statute requires the answer to state new matter constituting a defense. It does not say when omission results in loss.

claims.claim: Read the response form before filing.
claims.note: The cited PLD-050 item 2 was not supplied; neither statute gives this instruction.

flags.text: “Too old” omits the distinction between a debt's age and expiration of the period for bringing a covered action.
The sources do not establish commonness, proof requirements for ownership or amount, service challenges, or the consequences of omitting a defense.
PLD-050 item 2 cannot be checked against the form itself.
“Read the response form and ask for help before you file” directs the reader personally.

result.summary: Section 337 supports a time bar for covered actions. Section 431.30 distinguishes denials from new matter constituting a defense; it does not verify the defense list or the warning about loss.
